questions.question: How did you build the event discovery experience?
questions.whyAsked: The interviewer wants to understand how you implement user-facing features.
answerOutline: Describe the reusable React and TypeScript components in CampusConnect.
Explain how users can discover, filter, and register for events.

questions.question: How did you connect the application to its APIs?
questions.whyAsked: The interviewer wants to understand your backend integration experience.
answerOutline: Discuss the REST endpoints built with Node.js and Express.
Explain how the endpoints manage events and participant records.

questions.question: How did you work with persistent data?
questions.whyAsked: The interviewer wants to learn how you model and validate application data.
answerOutline: Describe PostgreSQL data models for event details.
Mention validation for attendance limits and registration status.

questions.question: How did you make the room finder easier to use?
questions.whyAsked: The interviewer wants to learn how you handle search and filtering.
answerOutline: Describe searchable room listings.
Explain the filters for building, capacity, equipment, and available time.

questions.question: How would you approach a technology you have not used before?
questions.whyAsked: The interviewer wants to understand how you handle a skill gap.
answerOutline: Be clear about the skills you are still learning.
Connect the gap to related experience from your resume.

questions.question: What was a challenge in CampusConnect?
questions.whyAsked: The interviewer wants to understand your contribution and decision-making.
answerOutline: Situation: clubs needed a way to manage events.
Task: create discovery and registration features.
Action: build reusable components and supporting endpoints.
Result: describe the outcome in your own words.

questions.question: How did you make StudySpace search useful?
questions.whyAsked: The interviewer wants to learn how you approach product requirements.
answerOutline: Situation: students needed to find study rooms.
Task: make rooms searchable by useful criteria.
Action: add filters and clear loading and error states.
Result: describe the outcome in your own words.

questions.question: How do you respond to feedback?
questions.whyAsked: The interviewer wants to understand how you collaborate and improve.
answerOutline: Use an example from peer feedback on StudySpace.
Explain how feedback informed your work.

warnings: Question 2 was adjusted to stay grounded in your resume.
